body.statement:
For a foldwise support-cleaned coherent fit, put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\), coordinatewise.  If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), then \(P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n})\to1\).  On \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), every true-zero measurement cell is zero in \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\), the bounds
\[
 \|\bar M_A-M_A\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{A,\infty}+\tau_{S,n}),
 \qquad
 \|\bar M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{Z,\infty}+\tau_{S,n})
\]
hold without a beta-min condition on positive cells, and
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right].
\]
Thus the support-cleaned correction has no first-order structural-zero leakage term.
body.proof_tex:
By the support-cleaning algebra lemma, \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) has all of the asserted deterministic consequences.  Moreover,
\[
 P(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}^{\mathsf c})
 =P\!\left(\frac{r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}}{\tau_{S,n}}>1\right)
 \longrightarrow0
\]
because \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).

It remains to prove the conditional-zero bound.  All fitted objects below are recomputed from \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\); in particular \(\widehat B=\bar M_A\odot\bar M_Z\).  Both summands in \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\) lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\widehat N)=\ker(\widehat B^{\mathsf T})\): the first by definition of \(\widehat N\), and the second because every column of \(\widehat h=\widehat N\widehat c\) lies in that range.  Spectral thresholding changes only the coefficients of their linear combination.  Hence, cellwise,
\[
 \widehat B^{\mathsf T}\widehat k=0. \tag{1}
\]
Under three-view conditional independence, the true conditional cell law is \(d=Bw\).  Conditioning on \((Y,X)\), applying (1), and using \(g(y\mid x)w_j(y,x)=\pi_j(x)f_j(y\mid x)\) give
\[
 E_P(\widehat k\mid X=x)
 =\sum_{j=1}^{K}\pi_j(x)\int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \{B_{\cdot j}(x)-\widehat B_{\cdot j}(x)\}^{\mathsf T}
 \widehat k(y,x)\,d\nu(y). \tag{2}
\]
Write \(\Delta_A=M_A-\bar M_A\) and \(\Delta_Z=M_Z-\bar M_Z\).  Columnwise tensor algebra yields the exact identity
\[
 B_{\cdot j}-\widehat B_{\cdot j}
 =\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes M_{Z,\cdot j}
  +M_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}
  -\Delta_{A,\cdot j}\otimes\Delta_{Z,\cdot j}. \tag{3}
\]
The tangent-space completeness and finite-projector theorems imply
\[
 E_P(k\mid A,J,X)=0,
 \qquad E_P(k\mid Z,J,X)=0. \tag{4}
\]
Consider the term in (2)--(3) that is linear in \(\Delta_A\) and contains \(k\).  If \(M_A(x)_{aj}>0\), then (4), three-view conditional independence, and the dominated outcome law imply
\[
 \int_{\mathcal Y}f_j(y\mid x)
 \sum_zM_Z(x)_{zj}k_{az}(y,x)\,d\nu(y)=0. \tag{5}
\]
If \(M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), then on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\) also \(\bar M_A(x)_{aj}=0\), so \(\Delta_A(x)_{aj}=0\).  Thus the entire linear \(\Delta_A\)-term containing \(k\) is zero.  The symmetric use of the second equality in (4) proves the same fact for the linear \(\Delta_Z\)-term.  Notice that conditioning in (5) is used only on positive-probability cells; true-zero cells are handled algebraically.

Substitute \(\widehat k=k+(\widehat k-k)\) in the two linear terms of (3).  The preceding cancellations leave only two terms that are linear in a cleaned measurement error and linear in \(\widehat k-k\), plus the product term in \((\Delta_A,\Delta_Z)\).  Latent positivity, the cleaned half-margin conditions, boundedness of \(Y\), and \(\|\widehat G_{\tau_G}^{\dagger}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/\varepsilon\) give a uniform \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\) bound for \(k\) and \(\widehat k\).  Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz in (2), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz over \(P_X\), the fixed value of \(K\), and the cleaned \(L^2\) bounds from the support-cleaning algebra lemma therefore give
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right].
\]
This proves the claim.
body.justification: The support-cleaning map restores the exact conditional-zero cancellation without an oracle support and without a positive-cell beta-min condition.
body.gap: A diagnostic allowance alone left first-order bias on true structural-zero cells; the corrected lemma proves exact removal and quantifies the threshold perturbation.
body.consumer: It supplies the zero-leakage projection-mean bound used by the quadratic remainder.
